answer.text: Time decay — erosion of option value with time

explanation.text: The Logic: Theta is the option Greek that measures the rate at which an option's price declines as time to expiry shortens, holding all other variables constant. Because an option's time-value component shrinks as expiry approaches, theta is typically negative for long option holders — they lose a little value each day from time decay alone. Theta increases (becomes more negative per day) as expiry nears. The Trap: Volatility sensitivity is vega. Interest-rate sensitivity is rho. Sensitivity to a unit move in the underlying is delta. Each Greek isolates a different driver of option value. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook (Sep 2025) covers options broadly in its derivatives chapter (pages 70-78) but does not specifically define option Greeks such as theta or the concept of time decay. The definition above is general option-pricing knowledge consistent with NISM-Series-VIII Equity Derivatives.
